# mame-mcp tool reference

51 tools. Generated from the running server's `tools/list`.

Legend: **read-only** never changes emulation state · *mutating* changes it safely ·
***destructive*** can corrupt the running program (memory writes, raw debugger commands).


## Session lifecycle

### `session.list_drivers`

*read-only* — Search the drivers compiled into this MAME binary by name or description.

  - `filter`?: string — Case-insensitive substring match.
  - `limit`?: number

### `session.start`

*mutating* — Launch MAME headless for a driver with the debugger active. Must be called before any other tool.

  - `driver`: string — Driver short name, e.g. "gridlee". Use session.list_drivers to find one.
  - `sound`?: boolean — Enable the sound backend. Leave false for headless; WAV capture works either way.
  - `seconds_to_run`?: number — Auto-exit after N emulated seconds (a useful watchdog).
  - `extra_args`?: array — Additional raw MAME command-line arguments.

### `session.status`

*read-only* — Whether MAME is running, the execution state, and the tail of its output log.

  - `log_lines`?: number

### `session.stop`

***destructive*** — Terminate the running MAME process.

_(no arguments)_


## Machine inspection

### `machine.describe`

*read-only* — The memory map the driver already knows: CPUs and their address spaces, ROM regions, RAM shares, screens. Call this first -- it saves reverse-engineering what MAME can just tell you.

_(no arguments)_

### `machine.reset`

***destructive*** — Reset the emulated machine. Soft reset by default; pass hard=true for a full power cycle.

  - `hard`?: boolean


## Execution control

### `exec.pause`

*mutating* — Pause the scheduler. Screenshots and memory reads still work while paused.

_(no arguments)_

### `exec.resume`

*mutating* — Resume from a breakpoint or pause. Pair with exec.wait_for_stop to catch the next trap.

_(no arguments)_

### `exec.run_for`

*mutating* — Advance a bounded amount of emulated time. The safest way to "let it run a bit".

  - `milliseconds`?: number

### `exec.run_to`

*mutating* — Resume until the PC reaches an address.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `address`: string,number — Target address.

### `exec.run_until_interrupt`

*mutating* — Resume until an interrupt fires (optionally a specific IRQ line).

  - `irq`?: number

### `exec.run_until_vblank`

*mutating* — Resume until the next vertical blank.

_(no arguments)_

### `exec.state`

*read-only* — Whether the CPU is running, paused, or stopped at a breakpoint.

_(no arguments)_

### `exec.step`

*mutating* — Execute N instructions (steps into calls).

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `count`?: number

### `exec.step_out`

*mutating* — Run until the current subroutine returns.

_(no arguments)_

### `exec.step_over`

*mutating* — Execute N instructions, stepping over subroutine calls.

  - `count`?: number

### `exec.wait_for_stop`

*read-only* — Block until the CPU hits a breakpoint/watchpoint or the timeout expires. Returns the stop reason, the trapped index, the PC and the device. Implemented in the supervisor, so it never blocks the emulator.

  - `timeout_ms`?: number — Default 10000.


## Breakpoints

### `bp.clear`

*mutating* — Clear one breakpoint by index, or all of them.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `index`?: number

### `bp.disable`

*mutating* — Disable one breakpoint by index, or all.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `index`?: number

### `bp.enable`

*mutating* — Enable one breakpoint by index, or all.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `index`?: number

### `bp.list`

*read-only* — All breakpoints, across every CPU unless a device is given.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.

### `bp.set`

*mutating* — Break when the PC reaches an address. Conditions are full debugger expressions, e.g. "{A}==5".

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `address`: string,number — Address to break on.
  - `condition`?: string — Debugger expression; the breakpoint only fires when true.
  - `action`?: string — Debugger command to run automatically on hit.


## Watchpoints

### `wp.clear`

*mutating* — Clear one watchpoint by index, or all.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `index`?: number

### `wp.list`

*read-only* — Watchpoints for a device and address space.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `space`?: string — Address space (default "program").

### `wp.set`

*mutating* — Break when a memory range is read and/or written. The primary tool for "what code touches this address?" -- combine with cpu.registers on the stop to identify the writer.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `space`?: string — Address space (default "program").
  - `address`: string,number — Start address of the watched range.
  - `length`?: number — Bytes to watch (default 1).
  - `type`?: string — Trap on read, write, or both (default "w").
  - `condition`?: string
  - `action`?: string


## Registerpoints

### `rp.clear`

*mutating* — Clear one registerpoint by index, or all.

  - `index`?: number

### `rp.set`

*mutating* — Break when an expression becomes true, e.g. "A==0x10". Evaluated every instruction, so it is slow but powerful.

  - `condition`: string
  - `action`?: string


## Memory

### `mem.list_regions`

*read-only* — Memory regions with sizes and widths. Regions are the raw ROM contents, unaffected by banking.

_(no arguments)_

### `mem.list_shares`

*read-only* — Shared RAM blocks. These are usually the actual videoram/spriteram/colorram.

_(no arguments)_

### `mem.read`

*read-only* — Read an address range. Returns base64 plus a hex+ASCII dump. Only coherent while the CPU is stopped.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `space`?: string — Address space (default "program").
  - `address`: string,number — Start address.
  - `length`?: number — Bytes to read (default 256, max 1MB).
  - `element_size`?: number
  - `mode`?: string

### `mem.region_read`

*read-only* — Read directly from a ROM region by tag. Unlike mem.read this bypasses banking and the CPU address map, so it is the right tool for static disassembly and graphics extraction.

  - `tag`: string — Region tag, e.g. ":maincpu" or ":gfx1".
  - `offset`?: string,number
  - `length`?: number

### `mem.search`

*read-only* — Find a byte pattern or ASCII string in an address range. Use this to locate strings, tables and known values, then watchpoint the hits.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `space`?: string — Address space (default "program").
  - `text`?: string — ASCII string to find.
  - `data`?: string — base64 byte pattern.
  - `bytes`?: array
  - `start`?: string,number
  - `end`?: string,number
  - `limit`?: number

### `mem.write`

***destructive*** — Write bytes to an address. Modifies emulation state.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `space`?: string — Address space (default "program").
  - `address`: string,number — Start address.
  - `data`?: string — base64 payload.
  - `bytes`?: array — Byte values, as an alternative to base64.


## CPU state and disassembly

### `cpu.disassemble`

*read-only* — Disassemble N instructions from an address (defaults to the current PC). Returns structured {address, bytes, text} entries rather than a text blob, so you can build a call graph from it.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `address`?: string,number — Defaults to the current PC.
  - `count`?: number — Instruction count (default 16).

### `cpu.list`

*read-only* — Every executable device with an address space.

_(no arguments)_

### `cpu.registers`

*read-only* — All register values for a device. Most useful while stopped at a breakpoint.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.

### `cpu.set_register`

***destructive*** — Write a register value.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `name`: string
  - `value`: string,number


## Expressions

### `sym.eval`

*read-only* — Evaluate a MAME debugger expression, e.g. "pc+4", "b@0x1000", "{A}".

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `expression`: string


## Annotations

### `annot.add`

*mutating* — Attach a comment to an address. MAME persists these per-ROM, so they are your disassembly notebook and survive across sessions.

  - `device`?: string — Device tag, e.g. ":maincpu". Defaults to the debugger's visible CPU.
  - `address`: string,number — Address to annotate.
  - `text`: string

### `annot.save`

*mutating* — Persist comments to the ROM comment file.

_(no arguments)_


## Video

### `video.screens`

*read-only* — Screens with resolution, refresh rate and frame counter.

_(no arguments)_

### `video.screenshot`

*read-only* — Capture the current frame as a PNG and return it inline. Works fully headless -- no X server or window is involved.

  - `screen`?: string — Screen tag; defaults to all active screens.
  - `filename`?: string


## Audio

### `audio.record_start`

*mutating* — Begin recording emulated audio to a .wav file. Works even with the sound backend disabled.

  - `filename`?: string

### `audio.record_stop`

*mutating* — Stop recording and report the resulting file.

_(no arguments)_


## Input

### `input.list_ports`

*read-only* — Input ports and fields (coins, start, buttons, DIP switches).

_(no arguments)_

### `input.press`

*mutating* — Hold an input field for N frames, then release it automatically.

  - `port`: string — Port tag from input.list_ports.
  - `field`: string — Field name from input.list_ports.
  - `frames`?: number — Frames to hold (default 2).
  - `value`?: number


## Save states

### `state.load`

***destructive*** — Restore machine state from a slot.

  - `slot`?: string

### `state.save`

*mutating* — Snapshot machine state to a slot for later restore.

  - `slot`?: string


## Escape hatch and logs

### `debug.command`

***destructive*** — Execute any MAME debugger command and return its console output (bpset, wpset, dasm, find, trace, trackpc, cheatinit, ...). Use this when no dedicated tool exists. Run "help" for the command list.

  - `command`: string — e.g. "trackpc 1,,1" or "find 0,ffff,\"HISCORE\""

### `debug.console_log`

*read-only* — Recent debugger console output, including anything produced by breakpoint actions.

  - `lines`?: number

### `debug.error_log`

*read-only* — The emulated machine's logerror() output. Drivers often name hardware registers here.

  - `lines`?: number
